[i]...what do we do? What do I do?[/i]

[i]Enquire with Felicia Stonetop at the bar, or with Sylvia Seafoam at the harbor.[/i]

[i]Hex of the Helmsman, by J. D. Wirman.[/i]

I wonder what's so interesting about it?

Where's anyone?
...just in case anyone missed the overt nautical theming.
A wooden carving of a fish skeleton.

Nobody's cleaned the floor in a while.

To move around, use the map button in the bottom left.
I think it's time to go outside.

It's been hung from the pipe,
so you can see it from the bed.

Old books...
Mostly fairy tales for young children.

My hair is perfect and does [h]not[/h] need fixing.

Would you mind not leaning on the fourth wall like that?

Stonetop Inn.
The Silkwirm Spectator.[/i]

[i]The Silkwirm Serpent[i].

Five stars. Nice and quiet. Would sleep on floor again.

The Best Inn in Silkwirm-on-Sea.[/i]

...maybe it's better that we don't know.

We have to rotate the glass orbs so the red and white balls [i]match[/i] the solutions on the screens.
So there's [i]four rows[/i], with labels off to the left... and [i]six columns[/i], with labels up at the top.

So when we place a tile, it has to work for the row [h]and[/h] the column it's in.
The labels for the [i]columns[/i] refer to orientation... rotation... even mirroring?
The labels for the rows just seem to be card suits. That's simple enough.
So - there's twelve big keyholes - those are for pirate keys.

I noticed the pirates can [i]rotate[/i], too.
For each pirate key, there's a flag key that matches it.
...but the pirate keys also need to be in the right positions - in relation to the colored lighthouses.
Mhm. Specifically, when a certain [i]pirate[/i] is looking at a certain [i]lighthouse.[/i]
I think the flags represent [i]views,[/i] as seen by the pirates...
So we've gotta move the six panels to cover up the circuit board.
-there's a way to [i]rotate[/i] them, too, but it's kind of indirect.
Each panel's connected to a smaller circular part... but we don't need those to cover the circuit board.
No, but we [i]can[/i] use them to change the angle of the panels they're connected to.
They need to be laid out evenly on the circuit board - leaving a gap between each one.
And then we can fill those gaps with the panels from the other two sets.
I'd start with the pink set - the one with three panels.
There are four sets - and they all have a certain shape we need to match.
It's kinda like a crossword - but for shapes instead of words.
The sets labelled B, C and D are separate... but A overlaps with all of them.
So the solution to A has to agree with B, C and D...
-but we need to focus on a solution that solves [i]all[/i] the sets at the same time.
There may be a couple different ways to make the shapes for each set-
So there's four slots, and each one needs a compass to go in it.
The labels are all describing a particular compass, I guess?
I think we'd get more information about how each compass worked if we moved them around...
...and pay attention to the needles while you're doing it.
At least one of them doesn't seem to be a compass at all!
It's really all about the behaviour of the needles - relative to the position the compasses.
So - there's a drawing of each of the suspects... one of Mortuga... and ones of us, too.
Each one needs to be moved to the right place on the board...

Oh - and Mortuga probably shouldn't be in [h]any[/h] of the segments.
I'd say me, you and Mariana all need to be in the same segment.
So... we can swap the sails between the nine boats.
-and we can tap the boats to [i]turn[/i] them - making them face different directions on the grid.
Seems like the boats can only point in straight lines or diagonals - a bit like chess.
I think it's supposed to be a sequence - like a journey.
The start point is the arrow tile on the left side, and the end point is the red X.
...and the angle of each boat represents the [i]direction[/i] of that movement.
So we need to plot a journey, from boat to boat, going from the start point to the end point.
I think the numbers on the sails represent [i]movements[/i] on the grid...
There's a bunch of stuff we can fiddle with on the front of the safe...
...and on the back, there's some kind of display.
Turn the hat around while you're looking at the display on the back.
That'll give you a better idea of how it works.

I'd say start with the column with a total of [h]2[/h] - it's only got two inputs, so they both need to be set to [h]1.[/h]

Right - surely, it's the key to knowing where to put everything else.

...and then the glass lenses [i]change and warp[/i] those images.

Two of the lenses use magnification to make things larger or smaller...
